concepts.name: Floating-point representation
concepts.summary: Explain that computers store reals as finite-precision binary floating-point numbers with limited range and spacing, so most reals are only approximated.

concepts.name: Absolute and relative error
concepts.summary: Define and compute absolute and relative error between an exact and an approximate value.

concepts.name: Round-off versus truncation error
concepts.summary: Distinguish errors from finite-precision arithmetic from errors caused by approximating a process with a finite one.

concepts.name: Iterative approximation idea
concepts.summary: Understand that many problems are solved by generating a sequence of improving approximations until a stopping tolerance is met.

concepts.name: Bisection method
concepts.summary: Explain how bisection brackets a root of a continuous function with a sign change and halves the interval each step.

concepts.name: Machine epsilon
concepts.summary: Recall that machine epsilon gives the relative spacing of floating-point numbers near 1 and bounds relative rounding error.

misconceptions.text: Computers represent decimal numbers like 0.1 exactly.
A smaller absolute error always means a more accurate answer regardless of the size of the true value.
Round-off and truncation error are the same thing and both vanish with a better algorithm.

concepts.name: Newton's method for roots
concepts.summary: Implement Newton's iteration using the derivative and recognise when it converges quickly or fails.

concepts.name: Secant method
concepts.summary: Apply the secant iteration to find roots without computing derivatives.

concepts.name: Convergence tolerance and stopping criteria
concepts.summary: Choose and implement stopping tests based on step size, residual and iteration limits.

concepts.name: Polynomial interpolation
concepts.summary: Construct the polynomial through given data points using Lagrange or Newton form.

concepts.name: Trapezoidal and Simpson rules
concepts.summary: Approximate definite integrals with the composite trapezoidal and Simpson rules.

concepts.name: Finite difference derivatives
concepts.summary: Approximate derivatives with forward, backward and central difference formulas.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.summary: Solve a linear system by forward elimination and back substitution.

misconceptions.text: Newton's method converges to a root from any starting guess.
Making the step size h in a finite difference as small as possible always gives the best derivative estimate.
A small difference between successive iterates guarantees a small error in the root.

concepts.name: Order of convergence analysis
concepts.summary: Determine and compare linear, superlinear and quadratic convergence of iterative methods from error sequences.

concepts.name: Truncation error via Taylor series
concepts.summary: Derive error orders of difference and quadrature formulas using Taylor expansions.

concepts.name: LU factorization with pivoting
concepts.summary: Factor a matrix as PA=LU and reuse the factors to solve multiple right-hand sides while avoiding unstable pivots.

concepts.name: Condition number
concepts.summary: Analyse how sensitive a problem's output is to input perturbations, including matrix condition number.

concepts.name: Numerical stability of algorithms
concepts.summary: Distinguish ill-conditioned problems from unstable algorithms and identify causes such as cancellation.

concepts.name: Splines and interpolation error
concepts.summary: Explain why high-degree equispaced polynomial interpolation oscillates and when piecewise splines are preferable.

concepts.name: Gaussian quadrature
concepts.summary: Apply Gauss-Legendre rules and explain why optimally placed nodes give higher exactness degree.

concepts.name: Iterative linear solvers
concepts.summary: Implement Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterations and check convergence via diagonal dominance.

misconceptions.text: A tiny residual guarantees an accurate solution of a linear system.
Using higher-degree interpolating polynomials always improves accuracy.
Gaussian elimination without pivoting is safe whenever the matrix is nonsingular.

concepts.name: Error budgeting and method selection
concepts.summary: Evaluate competing methods against accuracy, cost, robustness and problem structure and justify a choice.

concepts.name: Adaptive quadrature
concepts.summary: Analyse how error estimates drive adaptive subdivision for integrands with local difficulty.

concepts.name: Hybrid root finders
concepts.summary: Evaluate combinations of bracketing and fast methods that retain guaranteed convergence.

concepts.name: Krylov and conjugate gradient methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how Krylov subspace methods solve large sparse systems and how convergence depends on spectrum.

concepts.name: Preconditioning
concepts.summary: Evaluate preconditioners that reduce effective condition number to speed iterative convergence.

concepts.name: Least squares via QR and SVD
concepts.summary: Compare normal equations, QR and SVD for least squares in terms of stability and rank deficiency.

concepts.name: Sparse matrix computation
concepts.summary: Analyse storage formats and fill-in effects on cost of direct solvers for sparse systems.

concepts.name: Richardson extrapolation
concepts.summary: Use error expansions to combine coarse and fine results into higher-order estimates and diagnose convergence.

misconceptions.text: Solving least squares through the normal equations is as accurate as QR.
Conjugate gradient works for any square matrix.
Adaptive methods always beat fixed-step methods regardless of integrand smoothness or cost.

concepts.name: Backward error analysis
concepts.summary: Evaluate algorithms by proving or assessing that computed results are exact for slightly perturbed inputs.

concepts.name: Verification and validation of numerics
concepts.summary: Design convergence studies and tests with known solutions to verify implementations and error claims.

concepts.name: Designing custom numerical algorithms
concepts.summary: Create tailored schemes that exploit problem structure such as symmetry, singularities or oscillation.

concepts.name: Mixed-precision strategies
concepts.summary: Design workflows combining low- and high-precision arithmetic, such as iterative refinement, balancing speed and accuracy.

concepts.name: Eigenvalue algorithms
concepts.summary: Evaluate power, inverse and QR-based eigenvalue methods for accuracy, cost and structure.

concepts.name: Interval and rigorous error bounds
concepts.summary: Assess when guaranteed enclosures are needed and what they cost compared to heuristic error estimates.

concepts.name: Performance-aware numerical software
concepts.summary: Create implementations that balance accuracy with memory access, parallelism and library use such as BLAS and LAPACK.

misconceptions.text: Double precision is always enough, so numerical error can be ignored in production code.
If a convergence plot shows the expected order, the implementation is proven correct.
Hand-written algorithms are generally preferable to established libraries for performance.
